control_implications.evidence_excerpt: A flaw in NGINX's HTTP/2 support can allow an attacker to run code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled, without needing to log in. The decade-old flaw, CVE-2026-123007, dubbed "nginx2root," has been present in NGINX's open-source code since version 1.9.5, released on September 22, 2015. control_implications.headline: NGINX's HTTP/2 support enables unauthenticated code execution
control_implications.significance: This decade-old vulnerability in a ubiquitous web server component weakens assurance that asset inventories capture long-standing exposures. The accountable owner should confirm that all NGINX instances with HTTP/2 enabled have been identified and patched to fixed versions.

paragraphs.text: Active exploitation of critical vulnerabilities in widely deployed infrastructure components including NGINX, Apache Roller, Perforce Puppet, and F5 BIG-IP demands immediate asset identification and remediation verification across internet-facing and internal systems. The addition of Perforce Puppet to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog elevates urgency for configuration management platforms that underpin automated environments.

Supply chain compromises affecting Microsoft's official Agent Framework Python package on PyPI and a reported cyberattack on IT provider Wellington IT extend risk to dependent organizations, requiring supplier assurance reviews and software composition analysis validation. These events demonstrate how single points of failure in shared services and trusted repositories can cascade across multiple entities.
